newsitem.title: USA: Tobacco negotiators give White House update.
newsitem.headline: Tobacco negotiators give White House update.

text.p: Negotiators for tobacco companies and anti-smoking forces gave the White House an update on their settlement talks Wednesday, but reported that no deal was imminent.

White House deputy counsel Bruce Lindsey met with Mississippi Attorney General Michael Moore and several lawyers representing the tobacco companies and plaintiffs who have sued the industry, a White House official said.

Negotiators had met Sunday and Monday in Chicago. The talks began about two weeks ago between top industry executives and an array of anti-tobacco leaders. Published reports have said the industry might pay as much as $300 billion over 25 years into a compensation fund for smokers who fall sick with lung cancer and other diseases.
In return, the tobacco industry would get broad shelter from lawsuits and higher stock market valuations on their thriving tobacco and non-smoking businesses.
"They have not reached a settlement," said a White House official who said the parties met with Lindsey for about an hour.
The official described the parties as "deep into the negotiations" but that one participant in the White House meeting did not believe a settlement was imminent.
